title: From an agent to an interoperable MCP architecture

steps.title: 1 · Identify responsibilities
steps.question: What are an agent, an MCP client, a server, and a workflow?
steps.method: Explore the four occurrences and their definitions; distinguish roles from implementations.
steps.expected: Four roles identified, without claiming MCP conformance.

steps.title: 2 · Understand interactions
steps.question: Which interactions connect the architectural components?
steps.method: Examine uses, protocol-connection, and invokes in the direct composition.
steps.expected: Three illustrative connections identified and distinguished from parts.

steps.title: 3 · Explore assembly without transitivity
steps.question: Which parts are defined directly by each assembly?
steps.method: Open the illustrative assembly and inspect PartDefinition and PartUsage.
steps.expected: Direct usages are distinguished from recursive navigation paths.

steps.title: 4 · Examine a baseline
steps.question: Which realizations are declared, and what evidence is missing?
steps.method: Choose baseline:reference; inspect occ:ref-client and compare it with occ:ref-server.
steps.expected: An illustrative selection for the client; no implicit internal selection for the server.

steps.title: 5 · Run a local experiment
steps.question: What does an observed client/server message sequence demonstrate?
steps.method: Run node scripts/voyage-mcp-fixture.mjs; observe the messages and their result.
steps.expected: A deterministic JSON trace; this simulator is neither an MCP SDK nor a conformance test.

steps.title: 6 · Consolidate observations
steps.question: What have we demonstrated, and what remains to be tested?
steps.method: Compare hypotheses, the local trace, and references; distinguish declarations, observations, and conformance.
steps.expected: Knowledge status: declared roles, observed scenario, actual compatibility not established.
